Limited long-distance communication, mainly telegraph and letters
Travel by steamship and early airplanes, but no modern cars or electronic surveillance

institution: Private detectives and Secret Service; also includes private investigators and police
crime_subtype: complex inheritance and identity deception intertwined with murder

surface_summary: A complex tale of lost diamonds, secret identities, and mysterious deaths unfolds among a group of interconnected characters gathered on the Barge of Haunted Lives. The apparent murder of Prince Maranotti and the disappearance of valuable gems lead to suspicions and accusations among a cast of enigmatic figures.
accepted_facts: Prince Maranotti was murdered at Basselanto.
Two large diamonds known as the Eyes of Rajiid’s Buddha were lost and later found.
Paula Trevison is the daughter of the late Prince Maranotti and has multiple suitors.
Simon Glyncamp, the mind-reader, was believed dead but survived a murder attempt.
inferred_conclusions: The Sentimental Gargoyle is the murderer of Prince Maranotti.
Paula Trevison is the wife of the Sentimental Gargoyle.
Simon Glyncamp’s death was natural and unrelated to the case.
mechanism_description: The murder of Prince Maranotti was committed by Alfred Ferguson (Lord Galonfield) in a struggle near a cliff, where the Prince was pushed or fell to his death. The complex deception involving lost diamonds and multiple identities was orchestrated by Ferguson to secure the inheritance and win Paula Trevison’s hand. The mind-reader Glyncamp manipulated events but was ultimately killed by the Nervous Physician, who acted in self-defense.
delivery_path: Ferguson obtains one diamond and creates paste counterfeits.
He sends Forsythe to India to retrieve the second diamond unknowingly.
Ferguson orchestrates surveillance and uses Glyncamp to manipulate others.
Prince Maranotti is murdered by Ferguson during a confrontation.
Glyncamp is killed by the Nervous Physician during a post-mortem.
Paula Trevison’s identity and relationships are revealed on the barge.
Ferguson’s true identity and guilt are exposed.
outcome_result: Alfred Ferguson (Lord Galonfield) is revealed as the murderer of Prince Maranotti and the mastermind behind the diamond quest and identity deceptions.

false_assumption.statement: The Sentimental Gargoyle is the murderer of Prince Maranotti.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The Gargoyle was present at the scene and had a grotesque appearance that inspired suspicion. His hostile behavior and proximity to the victim made him a natural suspect.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It conceals the true murderer, Alfred Ferguson, who had a stronger motive and orchestrated events to implicate others.

supporting_points: He was seen near the murder scene at Basselanto.
His grotesque face and demeanor made him an object of suspicion.
He had a motive of jealousy and love for Paula Trevison.
He was hostile and defensive when questioned.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: Lack of direct evidence and eyewitness testimony confirming his guilt; the true murderer was later revealed to be Ferguson.

red_herrings.description: Simon Glyncamp, the American mind-reader, is suspected of manipulating events and possibly murdering Prince Maranotti.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: His mysterious powers and presence at key moments suggest involvement.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: He was ultimately killed by the Nervous Physician and was acting under duress and manipulation himself.

red_herrings.description: Rayon Demain, the handsome outlaw with a mysterious past, is suspected of violence and murder.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: His violent actions and connection to the burning of Mrs. Seaver’s house raise suspicion.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: His actions were driven by desperation and manipulation; he was not the murderer of Prince Maranotti.

closed_circle.rationale: All suspects are present on the Barge of Haunted Lives or closely connected to the events surrounding the murder and diamond quest, with no outsiders involved.

time_anchors: Night of the murder at Basselanto
Arrival of guests on the Barge of Haunted Lives
Date of the diamond recovery and disappearance
Date of Glyncamp’s apparent death and revival
time_windows: Interval between Prince Maranotti’s murder and the gathering on the barge
Period of the diamond quest in India and England
Time of Paula Trevison’s arrival and stay on the barge
access_objects: Diamonds known as the Eyes of Rajiid’s Buddha
authority_sources: Legal authority of the solicitor Ormond Dulmer
Medical authority of the Nervous Physician
Social authority of Prince Maranotti and Lord Galonfield

inference_path.observation: The Sentimental Gargoyle was seen near the murder scene and acted suspiciously.
inference_path.correction: His presence was explained by his attendance at the barge and unrelated hostility.
inference_path.effect: He is cleared as the murderer.
required_evidence: Eyewitness testimony placing Gargoyle at the barge during the murder
Lack of physical evidence linking Gargoyle to the murder weapon

inference_path.observation: Glyncamp was reported dead but appeared alive during the post-mortem.
inference_path.correction: He suffered from catalepsy and was killed later by the Nervous Physician.
inference_path.effect: His death is confirmed as murder, but not related to Prince Maranotti’s murder.
required_evidence: Medical examination records of Glyncamp’s catalepsy
Post-mortem report and eyewitness account of the murder

inference_path.observation: Paula Trevison’s multiple marriages and identity confusion suggest deception.
inference_path.correction: Her marriages are legally complex but she is a victim, not a culprit.
required_evidence: Testimonies from Paula and witnesses about her relationships

inference_path.observation: The diamonds were lost and recovered with counterfeit copies made.
inference_path.correction: The real diamonds were in Ferguson’s possession and used to manipulate others.
inference_path.effect: Ferguson’s motive and opportunity are established.
required_evidence: Safe-deposit box records and counterfeit stones
Correspondence between Ferguson and his solicitor Dulmer

inference_path.observation: Prince Maranotti died from a fall at the cliff with signs of struggle.
inference_path.correction: Ferguson caused the fall during a confrontation.
inference_path.effect: Ferguson is identified as the murderer.
required_evidence: Witness testimony from the Homicidal Professor who saw the struggle
Physical evidence of the struggle at the cliff

inference_path.observation: The Gargoyle’s death follows the revelation of Paula’s identity.
inference_path.correction: His death is natural or due to injuries from the struggle, not murder.
inference_path.effect: No foul play by others in Gargoyle’s death.
required_evidence: Medical report on Gargoyle’s cause of death
Testimony from Paula and witnesses at the barge

inference_path.observation: The Nervous Physician killed Glyncamp during the post-mortem.
inference_path.correction: The killing was in self-defense during a sudden attack.
inference_path.effect: Nervous Physician is not guilty of premeditated murder.
required_evidence: Eyewitness account of the attack during the post-mortem
Medical and legal records of the incident

discriminating_test.design: A careful reenactment of the struggle at the cliff is arranged, with witnesses and physical evidence examined to confirm the sequence of events and identify the assailant. The presence of the Homicidal Professor as an eyewitness is crucial to verify the true cause of Prince Maranotti’s death.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This reenactment reveals that Alfred Ferguson was the only person who could have caused the Prince’s fatal fall, disproving suspicions against others.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The reenactment must show that only Ferguson had the opportunity and means to push the Prince from the cliff.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given detailed narratives from multiple characters, including eyewitness accounts and physical descriptions of the crime scene. Clues such as the presence of counterfeit diamonds, the timeline of events, and the motives of each suspect are provided. The final confession and the reenactment clarify the true sequence of events, allowing attentive readers to deduce the culprit.

anchors.claim: Colonel Canbeck was a solitary duckhunter with one eye
anchors.anchor: The hunter was a thick-set, sullen-looking man, with a broad, clean-shaven face and thick, curly gray hair. He had only one eye

anchors.claim: Paula Trevison arrived at the barge veiled and was called the Veiled Aeronaut
anchors.anchor: the Veiled Aeronaut is now a member of our company

anchors.claim: Alfred Ferguson is actually Cecil, Lord Galonfield
anchors.anchor: Though, for reasons which you will soon understand, I have been known recently by the name of Alfred Ferguson, I am no other than Cecil, Lord Galonfield

anchors.claim: The lost diamonds are called the Eyes of Rajiid’s Buddha
anchors.anchor: For these gems most women--aye, even those who wear queenly crowns--would sell their very souls. They are the lost eyes of Rajiid’s Buddha

anchors.claim: Prince Maranotti was murdered and his body found at the foot of a cliff
anchors.anchor: Prince Maranotti had been murdered at Basselanto only a few hours before! The dead man’s body, bruised and scratched, apparently by human hands, had been found at the foot of a cliff

anchors.claim: Simon Glyncamp was believed dead but revived during a post-mortem
anchors.anchor: My consternation may easily be imagined when I saw Glyncamp, sitting almost upright on the operating table, and supported by Felkner

anchors.claim: The Sentimental Gargoyle was suspected but is innocent of the murder
anchors.anchor: That the cataleptic mind-reader was right when he accused you of his murder is a fact that is clear to all of us.

anchors.claim: The Homicidal Professor witnessed the murder of Prince Maranotti
anchors.anchor: I am the only person who saw Prince Maranotti die at the hands of his assassin.

anchors.claim: The diamonds were hidden in a jade image and a lead cylinder
anchors.anchor: I thrust into the inner pocket of my coat a hard, oblong object that was sewed in a little bag of oiled silk which exhaled the odor of fragrant spices

anchors.claim: The safe-deposit box seals were broken before the jaboowallah opened it
anchors.anchor: Glancing at the box as my companion drew it out, I saw that the seals, which Ferguson had affixed to the bundle, were broken.

anchors.claim: Paula Trevison is the daughter of the late Prince Maranotti
anchors.anchor: I am the daughter of the late Prince Maranotti.

anchors.claim: The seaplane left Paula Trevison stranded near the barge
anchors.anchor: I came in the seaplane... compelled to alight, however.

anchors.claim: The Gargoyle died after revealing the truth about the diamonds and Paula
anchors.anchor: The Gargoyle fell to the floor... The Gargoyle took her hands. Good-night, my Princess.

anchors.claim: The Nervous Physician is the murderer of Simon Glyncamp
anchors.anchor: Dr. Felkner, beginning the operation with a deep, rapid incision, had inflicted a mortal wound.

anchors.claim: The jaboowallah tortured Ferguson and cut Forsythe’s vocal cords
anchors.anchor: Having been brought to India... I was compelled to seat myself... I was decapitated... I had my vocal cords cut.

anchors.claim: Rayon Demain was a wild man raised in the wilderness
anchors.anchor: Rayon Demain, a young man raised in the wilderness, husband of Paula.

anchors.claim: The Hypochondriacal Painter raised Rayon Demain and taught him he was a god
anchors.anchor: I took the infant... I told him that this child was Rayon Demain--the son of the Great Spirit.

anchors.claim: The burning of Mrs. Seaver’s house was caused by Glenagassett
anchors.anchor: It was this Indian who had lighted the fire that destroyed Mrs. Seaver’s buildings.

anchors.claim: The final confession reveals Alfred Ferguson as the murderer
anchors.anchor: It is unfortunate that the endings of many true love stories should be so uncertain... the story may be said to be scarcely more than begun.
